programme.displayName: Amazon S3: Secure Storage and Integrated Event Workflows
programme.subtitle: Build secure object storage, recovery, event processing, private delivery, and audit workflows.
programme.description: Start with no training infrastructure and build six connected Amazon S3 labs in eu-west-2. Create secure access, private encrypted storage, version recovery and lifecycle rules, Lambda and SQS processing, SNS and EventBridge routing, CloudFront private delivery, CloudTrail and Athena auditing, and a complete dependency-safe teardown.
programme.learningOutcome: Create, secure, operate, integrate, monitor, audit, and completely remove an Amazon S3 workload using both the AWS Management Console and AWS CLI while explaining the related SAA-C03 architecture choices.

tasks.title: Create secure S3 training access
tasks.goal: Create a dedicated fa-s3-user, a temporary training policy, and a named fa-s3 CLI profile without using the root user for routine work.
tasks.whyItMatters: SAA-C03 expects secure human access, least privilege, role separation, and verification of the active AWS identity before resources are changed.

consoleSteps.title: Create the temporary training policy
consoleSteps.instruction: Sign in with an existing administrator-capable identity; do not use the root user for routine lab work.

instructions.text: Sign in with an existing administrator-capable identity; do not use the root user for routine lab work.
Open IAM from the AWS Console search bar.
In the left navigation, choose Policies, then choose Create policy.
Choose the JSON editor.
Replace <ACCOUNT_ID> with the 12-digit account ID shown in the Console account menu.
Replace the editor content with the complete policy JSON shown below.
Choose Next.
Enter fa-s3-training-policy as the policy name.
Choose Create policy.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: IAM lists fa-s3-training-policy as a customer-managed policy.
consoleSteps.warning: This broad temporary training policy is for the named fa-s3 resources only. Delete it in the final cleanup.

consoleSteps.title: Create and sign in as the training user
consoleSteps.instruction: In IAM, choose Users, then choose Create user.

instructions.text: In IAM, choose Users, then choose Create user.
Enter fa-s3-user as the user name.
Enable AWS Management Console access and use your normal secure temporary-password process.
Require a password change at first sign-in.
Finish creating the user.
Open fa-s3-user, choose Add permissions, then Attach policies directly.
Select only fa-s3-training-policy and complete the attachment.
Open the Security credentials tab and create one access key for Command Line Interface use.
Record the access key ID as [FA_S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID] and store the secret only in the AWS CLI credential prompt.
Sign out of the administrator and sign in as fa-s3-user.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The Console account menu identifies fa-s3-user and the temporary policy is attached.
consoleSteps.warning: Never put the secret access key in Author, source control, screenshots, commands, or chat.

cliSteps.command: aws sts get-caller-identity --profile [ADMIN_PROFILE]
cliSteps.explanation: Confirm the administrator profile and account before bootstrap.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The Account value is the intended AWS account and the ARN is not root.
cliSteps.warning: Stop if the account or identity is unexpected.

cliSteps.command: aws iam create-user --user-name fa-s3-user --profile [ADMIN_PROFILE]
cliSteps.explanation: Create the dedicated training IAM user.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The returned UserName is fa-s3-user.

cliSteps.command: aws iam create-policy --policy-name fa-s3-training-policy --policy-document file://fa-s3-training-policy.json --profile [ADMIN_PROFILE]
cliSteps.explanation: Create the supplied customer-managed policy after replacing <ACCOUNT_ID>.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The output contains the policy ARN; record it as [FA_S3_POLICY_ARN].

cliSteps.command: aws iam attach-user-policy --user-name fa-s3-user --policy-arn [FA_S3_POLICY_ARN] --profile [ADMIN_PROFILE]
cliSteps.explanation: Attach only the named training policy.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The command returns without an error.

cliSteps.command: aws iam create-access-key --user-name fa-s3-user --profile [ADMIN_PROFILE]
cliSteps.explanation: Create one temporary programmatic key.
cliSteps.expectedResult: Record the AccessKeyId as [FA_S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID] and configure the secret immediately.
cliSteps.warning: The secret is displayed once and must not be saved in the repository.

cliSteps.command: aws configure --profile fa-s3
cliSteps.explanation: Enter the temporary key, secret, eu-west-2, and json at the prompts.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The named fa-s3 profile is created locally.

cliSteps.command: aws sts get-caller-identity --profile fa-s3
cliSteps.explanation: Verify the training identity before creating resources.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The ARN ends with user/fa-s3-user and the Account value is correct.

verification.title: Confirm Console identity
verification.instruction: Open the account menu and inspect the signed-in identity.
verification.expectedResult: The identity is fa-s3-user, not root or the bootstrap administrator.

verification.title: Confirm CLI identity and Region
verification.instruction: Run get-caller-identity and aws configure get region --profile fa-s3.
verification.expectedResult: The identity is fa-s3-user and the Region is eu-west-2.

tasks.title: Create a private encrypted bucket and work with objects
tasks.feature: S3 buckets, objects, encryption, and public access controls
tasks.goal: Create one private general purpose bucket, upload harmless files, understand object keys, and prove that public access remains blocked.
tasks.whyItMatters: S3 security, bucket naming, object keys, encryption, and access controls are core SAA-C03 storage concepts.

consoleSteps.title: Create the private bucket
consoleSteps.instruction: Set the Console Region to eu-west-2.

instructions.text: Set the Console Region to eu-west-2.
Open Amazon S3 and choose General purpose buckets.
Choose Create bucket.
Leave Bucket type set to General purpose.
Enter fa-s3-foundations-<ACCOUNT_ID> as the globally unique bucket name.
Confirm Object Ownership is Bucket owner enforced.
Leave all four Block Public Access settings enabled.
Under Default encryption, select Server-side encryption with Amazon S3 managed keys (SSE-S3).
Enable Bucket Key only if the Console presents it for the selected encryption type.
Choose Create bucket.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The bucket fa-s3-foundations-<ACCOUNT_ID> is available in eu-west-2 and shows public access blocked.
consoleSteps.warning: Do not disable Block Public Access or use an existing bucket.

consoleSteps.title: Upload, inspect, download, and copy a harmless object
consoleSteps.instruction: Create a small local text file named hello-s3.txt containing no confidential information.

instructions.text: Create a small local text file named hello-s3.txt containing no confidential information.
Open fa-s3-foundations-<ACCOUNT_ID> and choose Create folder.
Enter foundations as the folder name and create it.
Open foundations and choose Upload.
Choose Add files and select hello-s3.txt.
Expand Properties and confirm the selected encryption setting uses the bucket default.
Choose Upload and wait for the success message.
Open the object and record its full key as foundations/hello-s3.txt.
Choose Download and verify the downloaded text.
Select the object, choose Actions, then Copy.
Set the destination key to foundations/hello-s3-copy.txt and finish the copy.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: Both foundations/hello-s3.txt and foundations/hello-s3-copy.txt appear and neither object is public.

cliSteps.command: aws s3api create-bucket --bucket fa-s3-foundations-<ACCOUNT_ID> --region eu-west-2 --create-bucket-configuration LocationConstraint=eu-west-2 --profile fa-s3
cliSteps.explanation: Create the named regional general purpose bucket.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The command returns a Location value.

cliSteps.command: aws s3api put-public-access-block --bucket fa-s3-foundations-<ACCOUNT_ID> --public-access-block-configuration BlockPublicAcls=true,IgnorePublicAcls=true,BlockPublicPolicy=true,RestrictPublicBuckets=true --profile fa-s3
cliSteps.explanation: Explicitly enable all four bucket public-access controls.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The command returns without an error.

cliSteps.command: aws s3api put-bucket-encryption --bucket fa-s3-foundations-<ACCOUNT_ID> --server-side-encryption-configuration Rules=[{ApplyServerSideEncryptionByDefault={SSEAlgorithm=AES256}}] --profile fa-s3
cliSteps.explanation: Set SSE-S3 as the bucket default encryption.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The command returns without an error.

cliSteps.command: aws s3 cp hello-s3.txt s3://fa-s3-foundations-<ACCOUNT_ID>/foundations/hello-s3.txt --profile fa-s3
cliSteps.explanation: Upload the harmless source object.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The upload line names foundations/hello-s3.txt.

cliSteps.command: aws s3api head-object --bucket fa-s3-foundations-<ACCOUNT_ID> --key foundations/hello-s3.txt --profile fa-s3
cliSteps.explanation: Inspect metadata without downloading the body.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response includes ContentLength, ETag, and ServerSideEncryption AES256.

cliSteps.command: aws s3api copy-object --bucket fa-s3-foundations-<ACCOUNT_ID> --copy-source fa-s3-foundations-<ACCOUNT_ID>/foundations/hello-s3.txt --key foundations/hello-s3-copy.txt --profile fa-s3
cliSteps.explanation: Create a second key from the first object.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response includes CopyObjectResult.

verification.title: Verify bucket protection
verification.instruction: Open Permissions and Default encryption for the bucket.
verification.expectedResult: All four public access settings are on and default encryption is SSE-S3.

verification.title: Verify object keys
verification.instruction: List the foundations prefix.
verification.expectedResult: The original and copy have distinct keys and the expected sizes.

tasks.title: Enable versioning and recover overwritten or deleted objects
tasks.goal: Create multiple versions of one object, recover an earlier version, and restore an object hidden by a delete marker.
tasks.whyItMatters: Versioning protects against accidental overwrites and deletions and is a foundation for replication and resilient S3 designs.

consoleSteps.title: Enable versioning and create two versions
consoleSteps.instruction: Open fa-s3-foundations-<ACCOUNT_ID>.

instructions.text: Open fa-s3-foundations-<ACCOUNT_ID>.
Choose Properties.
In Bucket Versioning, choose Edit.
Select Enable and save changes.
Return to Objects and open foundations.
Edit hello-s3.txt locally so the text clearly says version 2.
Upload it again using exactly the same key foundations/hello-s3.txt.
Turn on Show versions.
Confirm the object key has at least two different version IDs.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The same object key has a current version and an older noncurrent version.
consoleSteps.warning: After first enabling versioning, AWS advises allowing time for the setting to propagate before critical writes.

consoleSteps.title: Recover from overwrite and deletion
consoleSteps.instruction: With Show versions enabled, select the older version of foundations/hello-s3.txt.

instructions.text: With Show versions enabled, select the older version of foundations/hello-s3.txt.
Choose Download and confirm it contains the original text.
Turn off Show versions and delete foundations/hello-s3.txt.
Turn Show versions on again.
Find the delete marker for foundations/hello-s3.txt.
Select only that delete marker and choose Delete.
Confirm permanent deletion of the marker.
Turn Show versions off and open foundations/hello-s3.txt.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: Removing the delete marker makes the previous object version current and visible again.
consoleSteps.warning: Delete only the marker, not the retained object versions.

cliSteps.command: aws s3api put-bucket-versioning --bucket fa-s3-foundations-<ACCOUNT_ID> --versioning-configuration Status=Enabled --profile fa-s3
cliSteps.explanation: Enable bucket versioning.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The command returns without an error.

cliSteps.command: aws s3 cp hello-s3-v2.txt s3://fa-s3-foundations-<ACCOUNT_ID>/foundations/hello-s3.txt --profile fa-s3
cliSteps.explanation: Upload changed content under the existing key.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The upload completes.

cliSteps.command: aws s3api list-object-versions --bucket fa-s3-foundations-<ACCOUNT_ID> --prefix foundations/hello-s3.txt --profile fa-s3
cliSteps.explanation: List version IDs and current status.
cliSteps.expectedResult: At least two Versions entries have different VersionId values.

cliSteps.command: aws s3api delete-object --bucket fa-s3-foundations-<ACCOUNT_ID> --key foundations/hello-s3.txt --profile fa-s3
cliSteps.explanation: Create a delete marker rather than permanently deleting versioned data.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response includes DeleteMarker true and a VersionId; record it as [HELLO_DELETE_MARKER_ID].

cliSteps.command: aws s3api delete-object --bucket fa-s3-foundations-<ACCOUNT_ID> --key foundations/hello-s3.txt --version-id [HELLO_DELETE_MARKER_ID] --profile fa-s3
cliSteps.explanation: Remove only the recorded delete marker.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response confirms the marker version was deleted.

cliSteps.command: aws s3api head-object --bucket fa-s3-foundations-<ACCOUNT_ID> --key foundations/hello-s3.txt --profile fa-s3
cliSteps.explanation: Prove the earlier version is visible again.
cliSteps.expectedResult: Metadata is returned without a 404 error.

verification.title: Verify multiple versions
verification.instruction: Show versions for foundations/hello-s3.txt.
verification.expectedResult: Multiple unique version IDs remain available.

verification.title: Verify recovery
verification.instruction: Open or download the restored current object.
verification.expectedResult: The object is accessible after removal of only the delete marker.

tasks.title: Create lifecycle rules for cost and retention management
tasks.goal: Apply a lifecycle rule only to training objects and understand current-version transition, noncurrent-version expiration, and incomplete multipart cleanup.
tasks.whyItMatters: SAA-C03 regularly tests storage-class selection, lifecycle transitions, retention, and the effect of versioning on expiration.

consoleSteps.title: Create a prefix-scoped lifecycle rule
consoleSteps.instruction: Open fa-s3-foundations-<ACCOUNT_ID> and choose Management.

instructions.text: Open fa-s3-foundations-<ACCOUNT_ID> and choose Management.
Choose Create lifecycle rule.
Enter fa-s3-training-lifecycle as the rule name.
Choose Limit the scope to specific prefixes or tags.
Enter foundations/ as the prefix.
Select Transition current versions of objects between storage classes.
Choose Standard-IA and enter 30 days after object creation.
Select Permanently delete noncurrent versions of objects and enter 30 days after they become noncurrent.
Retain 1 newer noncurrent version if that field is available.
Select Delete incomplete multipart uploads and enter 7 days.
Review the timeline and choose Create rule.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: Management lists an enabled fa-s3-training-lifecycle rule scoped to foundations/.
consoleSteps.warning: Lifecycle actions are asynchronous and transition or minimum-storage charges may apply; this lab verifies configuration rather than waiting 30 days.

consoleSteps.title: Review lifecycle behaviour without waiting
consoleSteps.instruction: Open the lifecycle rule and review its current-version timeline.

instructions.text: Open the lifecycle rule and review its current-version timeline.
Confirm only keys beginning foundations/ match the rule.
Confirm current versions transition after 30 days rather than immediately.
Confirm old versions are permanently removed only after becoming noncurrent for 30 days.
Confirm unfinished multipart uploads are removed after 7 days.
Return to Objects and verify the current training objects still exist.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The learner can explain each action and the current objects remain available during the lab.

cliSteps.command: aws s3api put-bucket-lifecycle-configuration --bucket fa-s3-foundations-<ACCOUNT_ID> --lifecycle-configuration file://fa-s3-lifecycle.json --profile fa-s3
cliSteps.explanation: Apply the supplied prefix-scoped lifecycle JSON.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The command returns without an error.

cliSteps.command: aws s3api get-bucket-lifecycle-configuration --bucket fa-s3-foundations-<ACCOUNT_ID> --profile fa-s3
cliSteps.explanation: Retrieve the active rule.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response shows ID fa-s3-training-lifecycle, Prefix foundations/, and Status Enabled.

cliSteps.command: aws s3api list-objects-v2 --bucket fa-s3-foundations-<ACCOUNT_ID> --prefix foundations/ --profile fa-s3
cliSteps.explanation: Confirm lifecycle does not immediately remove current objects.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The expected training object keys remain listed.

verification.title: Verify rule scope
verification.instruction: Inspect the rule filter and timeline.
verification.expectedResult: Only foundations/ is targeted and every timing value matches the lab.

verification.title: Explain version-aware expiration
verification.instruction: Compare current-version transition with noncurrent-version expiration.
verification.expectedResult: The learner can state that deleting a current version in a versioned bucket normally creates a delete marker.

tasks.title: Process S3 uploads with Lambda
tasks.feature: S3 event notifications, Lambda, and CloudWatch Logs
tasks.goal: Invoke a small Lambda function when a file is uploaded under incoming/ and verify the event in CloudWatch Logs.
tasks.whyItMatters: Event-driven file processing is a common serverless pattern and SAA-C03 tests source permissions, Region alignment, and recursive-trigger prevention.

consoleSteps.title: Create the Lambda execution role and function
consoleSteps.instruction: Switch to the IAM console while remaining signed in as fa-s3-user.

instructions.text: Switch to the IAM console while remaining signed in as fa-s3-user.
Choose Roles, then Create role.
Choose AWS service and Lambda as the trusted use case.
Attach AWSLambdaBasicExecutionRole.
Name the role fa-s3-lambda-role and create it.
Open Lambda in eu-west-2 and choose Create function.
Choose Author from scratch.
Enter fa-s3-object-inspector as the function name.
Choose the latest supported Python 3 runtime offered by the Console.
Choose Use an existing role and select fa-s3-lambda-role.
Create the function.
Replace the code with the complete Python code shown below and choose Deploy.

jsonBlocks.title: lambda_function.py

consoleSteps.expectedResult: Lambda lists fa-s3-object-inspector with fa-s3-lambda-role and deployed code.
consoleSteps.warning: The function logs only bucket, key, size, and event name; do not upload confidential files.

consoleSteps.title: Add a prefix-filtered S3 trigger and test it
consoleSteps.instruction: Open fa-s3-object-inspector and choose Add trigger.

instructions.text: Open fa-s3-object-inspector and choose Add trigger.
Choose S3 as the source.
Select fa-s3-foundations-<ACCOUNT_ID>.
Select All object create events.
Enter incoming/ as the Prefix.
Acknowledge the recursive-invocation warning because this function writes no S3 objects.
Choose Add.
Upload a harmless file as incoming/lambda-test.txt.
Open Monitor, choose View CloudWatch logs, and open the newest log stream.
Find the JSON log line containing incoming/lambda-test.txt.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: CloudWatch Logs shows one processed S3 ObjectCreated event for incoming/lambda-test.txt.
consoleSteps.warning: Never configure an unfiltered trigger if the same function writes back into its triggering location.

cliSteps.command: aws iam create-role --role-name fa-s3-lambda-role --assume-role-policy-document file://lambda-trust-policy.json --profile fa-s3
cliSteps.explanation: Create the supplied Lambda trust role.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The output names fa-s3-lambda-role.

cliSteps.command: aws iam attach-role-policy --role-name fa-s3-lambda-role --policy-arn arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/service-role/AWSLambdaBasicExecutionRole --profile fa-s3
cliSteps.explanation: Allow the function to write CloudWatch Logs.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The command returns without an error.

cliSteps.command: Compress-Archive -Path lambda_function.py -DestinationPath fa-s3-object-inspector.zip -Force
cliSteps.explanation: Package only the supplied Lambda source file in PowerShell.
cliSteps.expectedResult: fa-s3-object-inspector.zip exists and contains lambda_function.py at its root.

cliSteps.command: aws lambda create-function --function-name fa-s3-object-inspector --runtime python3.13 --role arn:aws:iam::<ACCOUNT_ID>:role/fa-s3-lambda-role --handler lambda_function.lambda_handler --zip-file fileb://fa-s3-object-inspector.zip --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-s3
cliSteps.explanation: Create the function from the locally packaged supplied code.
cliSteps.expectedResult: State is Pending or Active; wait until Active.

cliSteps.command: aws lambda add-permission --function-name fa-s3-object-inspector --statement-id AllowS3Invoke --action lambda:InvokeFunction --principal s3.amazonaws.com --source-arn arn:aws:s3:::fa-s3-foundations-<ACCOUNT_ID> --source-account <ACCOUNT_ID> --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-s3
cliSteps.explanation: Allow only the named bucket to invoke the function.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response contains the AllowS3Invoke statement.

cliSteps.command: aws s3api put-bucket-notification-configuration --bucket fa-s3-foundations-<ACCOUNT_ID> --notification-configuration file://lambda-notification.json --profile fa-s3
cliSteps.explanation: Apply the supplied ObjectCreated notification filtered to incoming/.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The command returns without an error.

cliSteps.command: aws s3 cp lambda-test.txt s3://fa-s3-foundations-<ACCOUNT_ID>/incoming/lambda-test.txt --profile fa-s3
cliSteps.explanation: Upload a harmless trigger object.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The upload completes.

cliSteps.command: aws logs tail /aws/lambda/fa-s3-object-inspector --since 10m --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-s3
cliSteps.explanation: Read recent function logs.
cliSteps.expectedResult: A log line identifies incoming/lambda-test.txt.

verification.title: Verify filtered trigger
verification.instruction: Inspect the function trigger configuration.
verification.expectedResult: The bucket and incoming/ prefix are exact.

verification.title: Verify invocation
verification.instruction: Inspect the latest CloudWatch log stream.
verification.expectedResult: The harmless test object appears and there is no recursive loop.

tasks.title: Buffer S3 events through SQS and Lambda
tasks.feature: S3, SQS, dead-letter queues, and Lambda event source mappings
tasks.goal: Send S3 upload events to an SQS queue with a dead-letter queue and let Lambda consume the buffered messages.
tasks.whyItMatters: A queue decouples producers and consumers, absorbs traffic spikes, and supports controlled retry and failure handling.

consoleSteps.title: Create the dead-letter queue and source queue
consoleSteps.instruction: Open Amazon SQS in eu-west-2.

instructions.text: Open Amazon SQS in eu-west-2.
Choose Create queue and keep Standard selected.
Enter fa-s3-events-dlq and create the queue.
Record its ARN as [S3_EVENTS_DLQ_ARN].
Create another Standard queue named fa-s3-events-queue.
Expand Dead-letter queue.
Enable the dead-letter queue and select fa-s3-events-dlq.
Set Maximum receives to 3.
Create the source queue and record its ARN as [S3_EVENTS_QUEUE_ARN].
Open the source queue Access policy and add the supplied statement allowing only the named S3 bucket to call SendMessage.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: Both queues exist, the source queue targets the DLQ, and its policy grants the named bucket SendMessage.
consoleSteps.warning: Use Standard queues for direct S3 notifications; direct S3 notifications do not support SQS FIFO.

consoleSteps.title: Route queue/ uploads to SQS and connect Lambda
consoleSteps.instruction: Open the S3 bucket Properties tab.

instructions.text: Open the S3 bucket Properties tab.
Under Event notifications, choose Create event notification.
Enter fa-s3-to-sqs.
Enter queue/ as the Prefix.
Select All object create events.
Choose SQS queue as the destination and select fa-s3-events-queue.
Save the notification.
Open fa-s3-object-inspector in Lambda and choose Add trigger.
Choose SQS and select fa-s3-events-queue.
Keep batch size small at 1 for this training test and add the trigger.
Upload queue/buffer-test.txt to the S3 bucket.
Open the Lambda CloudWatch logs and verify an SQS event was received.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The S3 event travels through fa-s3-events-queue and invokes the Lambda consumer.
consoleSteps.warning: Adding an SQS trigger requires the Lambda execution role to have receive and delete permissions for the source queue.

cliSteps.command: aws sqs create-queue --queue-name fa-s3-events-dlq --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-s3
cliSteps.explanation: Create the dead-letter queue.
cliSteps.expectedResult: Record QueueUrl as [S3_EVENTS_DLQ_URL].

cliSteps.command: aws sqs create-queue --queue-name fa-s3-events-queue --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-s3
cliSteps.explanation: Create the source Standard queue.
cliSteps.expectedResult: Record QueueUrl as [S3_EVENTS_QUEUE_URL].

cliSteps.command: aws sqs set-queue-attributes --queue-url [S3_EVENTS_QUEUE_URL] --attributes file://sqs-redrive-and-policy.json --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-s3
cliSteps.explanation: Apply the supplied redrive policy and S3 SendMessage queue policy.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The command returns without an error.

cliSteps.command: aws iam attach-role-policy --role-name fa-s3-lambda-role --policy-arn arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/service-role/AWSLambdaSQSQueueExecutionRole --profile fa-s3

tasks.title: Fan out and route S3 events with SNS and EventBridge
tasks.feature: SNS fan-out and EventBridge event filtering
tasks.goal: Send a direct upload notification to SNS and route selected S3 deletion events through EventBridge to the same notification topic.
tasks.whyItMatters: SNS supports push fan-out while EventBridge provides content-based event routing; choosing between them and SQS is a key architecture skill.

consoleSteps.title: Create an SNS topic and confirmed email subscription
consoleSteps.instruction: Open Amazon SNS in eu-west-2.

instructions.text: Open Amazon SNS in eu-west-2.
Choose Topics, then Create topic.
Choose Standard and enter fa-s3-events-topic.
Create the topic and record its ARN as [S3_EVENTS_TOPIC_ARN].
Choose Create subscription.
Select Email as the protocol and enter an email address you control.
Create the subscription.
Open the confirmation email and confirm the subscription.
Return to SNS and verify the subscription status is Confirmed.
Edit the topic access policy so only the named S3 bucket and EventBridge can publish.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: SNS shows fa-s3-events-topic with a confirmed subscription and restricted publisher policy.
consoleSteps.warning: Email endpoints can receive messages during the test; remove the subscription during cleanup.

consoleSteps.title: Create direct SNS and EventBridge routes
consoleSteps.instruction: Open the S3 bucket Properties tab and create an event notification named fa-s3-to-sns.

instructions.text: Open the S3 bucket Properties tab and create an event notification named fa-s3-to-sns.
Use prefix notify/ and All object create events.
Choose SNS topic and select fa-s3-events-topic.
Save the notification.
In the Event notifications section, enable Amazon EventBridge for the bucket.
Open EventBridge in eu-west-2 and choose Rules.
Create a rule named fa-s3-delete-route on the default event bus.
Use an event pattern with source aws.s3, detail-type Object Deleted, and the exact bucket name.
Choose SNS topic fa-s3-events-topic as the target.
Create the rule.
Upload notify/sns-test.txt and confirm the direct SNS email.
Delete a harmless test object and confirm a separate EventBridge-routed message.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The email endpoint receives an upload notification and a separately routed deletion event.
consoleSteps.warning: Event delivery can be asynchronous and duplicate events are possible; consumers must be idempotent.

cliSteps.command: aws sns create-topic --name fa-s3-events-topic --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-s3
cliSteps.explanation: Create the Standard SNS topic.
cliSteps.expectedResult: Record TopicArn as [S3_EVENTS_TOPIC_ARN].

cliSteps.command: aws sns subscribe --topic-arn [S3_EVENTS_TOPIC_ARN] --protocol email --notification-endpoint [EMAIL_ADDRESS] --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-s3
cliSteps.explanation: Create the email subscription.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response shows pending confirmation until the email link is used.

cliSteps.command: aws s3api put-bucket-notification-configuration --bucket fa-s3-foundations-<ACCOUNT_ID> --notification-configuration file://combined-notifications.json --profile fa-s3
cliSteps.explanation: Apply the supplied complete notification configuration containing the retained Lambda, SQS, SNS, and EventBridge settings.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The command returns without an error.

cliSteps.command: aws events put-rule --name fa-s3-delete-route --event-pattern file://fa-s3-delete-event-pattern.json --state ENABLED --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-s3
cliSteps.explanation: Create the deletion-event rule.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The output contains the rule ARN.

cliSteps.command: aws events put-targets --rule fa-s3-delete-route --targets Id=SnsTarget,Arn=[S3_EVENTS_TOPIC_ARN] --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-s3
cliSteps.explanation: Attach SNS as the rule target.
cliSteps.expectedResult: FailedEntryCount is 0.

cliSteps.command: aws s3 cp sns-test.txt s3://fa-s3-foundations-<ACCOUNT_ID>/notify/sns-test.txt --profile fa-s3
cliSteps.explanation: Trigger the direct SNS upload path.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The upload succeeds and the confirmed endpoint receives a notification.

cliSteps.command: aws s3 rm s3://fa-s3-foundations-<ACCOUNT_ID>/notify/sns-test.txt --profile fa-s3

tasks.title: Deliver private S3 content through CloudFront
tasks.feature: CloudFront Origin Access Control and private S3 origins
tasks.goal: Serve a small website through CloudFront while direct anonymous access to its S3 objects remains blocked.
tasks.whyItMatters: CloudFront with OAC is the recommended pattern for securely delivering private S3 origin content at the edge.

consoleSteps.title: Upload website content and create the distribution
consoleSteps.instruction: Create a harmless local index.html that identifies this as the S3 training site.

instructions.text: Create a harmless local index.html that identifies this as the S3 training site.
Upload it to fa-s3-foundations-<ACCOUNT_ID> with the key site/index.html and Content-Type text/html.
Open CloudFront and choose Create distribution.
For Origin domain, select fa-s3-foundations-<ACCOUNT_ID>.s3.eu-west-2.amazonaws.com; do not choose the S3 website endpoint.
For Origin path, enter /site.
For Origin access, choose Origin access control settings (recommended).
Choose Create new OAC.
Name it fa-s3-oac and keep signing behaviour set to always sign requests.
Allow CloudFront to update the S3 bucket policy when offered, or copy the displayed policy for the next step.
Set Viewer protocol policy to Redirect HTTP to HTTPS.
Set Default root object to index.html.
Create the distribution and record its ID as [CLOUDFRONT_DISTRIBUTION_ID] and domain as [CLOUDFRONT_DOMAIN].

jsonBlocks.title: fa-s3-cloudfront-distribution.json

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The distribution deploys with the private S3 origin, /site path, OAC, HTTPS redirect, and index.html.

consoleSteps.title: Verify CloudFront-only access
consoleSteps.instruction: Open the S3 bucket Permissions tab.

instructions.text: Open the S3 bucket Permissions tab.
Confirm Block Public Access remains fully enabled.
Review the bucket policy statement granting only the CloudFront distribution service principal s3:GetObject access.
Wait until the distribution status is Deployed.
Open https://[CLOUDFRONT_DOMAIN]/ in a browser.
Confirm the training page loads over HTTPS.
Try the direct anonymous S3 object URL in a private browser window.
Confirm direct S3 access is denied.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: CloudFront serves index.html successfully while direct anonymous S3 access remains denied.
consoleSteps.warning: Do not make the bucket or objects public to fix a CloudFront error; correct OAC and bucket policy instead.

cliSteps.command: aws s3 cp index.html s3://fa-s3-foundations-<ACCOUNT_ID>/site/index.html --content-type text/html --profile fa-s3
cliSteps.explanation: Upload the website entry object.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The upload completes.

cliSteps.command: aws cloudfront create-origin-access-control --origin-access-control-config Name=fa-s3-oac,Description=Training-S3-OAC,SigningProtocol=sigv4,SigningBehavior=always,OriginAccessControlOriginType=s3 --profile fa-s3
cliSteps.explanation: Create the recommended OAC.
cliSteps.expectedResult: Record Id as [CLOUDFRONT_OAC_ID].

cliSteps.command: aws cloudfront create-distribution --distribution-config file://fa-s3-cloudfront-distribution.json --profile fa-s3
cliSteps.explanation: Create the distribution from the supplied configuration containing the exact S3 origin, /site path, OAC ID, HTTPS redirect, and default root object.
cliSteps.expectedResult: Record Distribution.Id and Distribution.DomainName.

cliSteps.command: aws s3api put-bucket-policy --bucket fa-s3-foundations-<ACCOUNT_ID> --policy file://fa-s3-cloudfront-bucket-policy.json --profile fa-s3

cliSteps.command: aws cloudfront get-distribution --id [CLOUDFRONT_DISTRIBUTION_ID] --profile fa-s3

tasks.title: Audit S3 object access with CloudTrail and Athena
tasks.feature: CloudTrail data events, Athena, and CloudWatch monitoring
tasks.goal: Record object-level S3 API activity, query the delivered records, and create a simple bucket-size monitoring view.
tasks.whyItMatters: SAA-C03 distinguishes audit records from operational metrics and expects architects to select CloudTrail, Athena, and CloudWatch appropriately.

consoleSteps.title: Create a trail with S3 data events
consoleSteps.instruction: Create a second private bucket named fa-s3-audit-<ACCOUNT_ID> in eu-west-2 with Block Public Access enabled and SSE-S3.

instructions.text: Create a second private bucket named fa-s3-audit-<ACCOUNT_ID> in eu-west-2 with Block Public Access enabled and SSE-S3.
Open CloudTrail and choose Trails.
Choose Create trail.
Enter fa-s3-audit-trail.
Choose the existing fa-s3-audit-<ACCOUNT_ID> bucket for log storage.
Keep log file validation enabled.
Under Event type, include Management events and Data events.
For Data event type, choose S3.
Use a selector limited to objects in arn:aws:s3:::fa-s3-foundations-<ACCOUNT_ID>/.
Include read and write object events.
Create the trail.
Upload, download, and delete one harmless object to generate PutObject, GetObject, and DeleteObject events.

jsonBlocks.title: fa-s3-data-events.json

consoleSteps.expectedResult: fa-s3-audit-trail is logging management and selected S3 object data events to the audit bucket.
consoleSteps.warning: CloudTrail data events and Athena queries can incur charges; generate only the few test events required.

consoleSteps.title: Create an Athena table and query object activity
consoleSteps.instruction: Wait for CloudTrail log delivery, then open Athena in eu-west-2.

instructions.text: Wait for CloudTrail log delivery, then open Athena in eu-west-2.
Open Query editor.
Set the query result location to s3://fa-s3-audit-<ACCOUNT_ID>/athena-results/.
Use the CloudTrail console action Create Athena table for the trail when available, or create the supplied external table.
Name the table fa_s3_cloudtrail_logs.
Run a query filtering eventSource = s3.amazonaws.com and the target bucket name.
Select eventTime, eventName, userIdentity.arn, requestParameters.bucketName, and requestParameters.key.
Order newest events first and limit the result to 20 rows.
Find the generated PutObject, GetObject, and DeleteObject events.
Open CloudWatch Metrics, choose S3, then Storage Metrics.
Locate BucketSizeBytes and NumberOfObjects for fa-s3-foundations-<ACCOUNT_ID> and explain that daily storage metrics differ from API audit events.

jsonBlocks.title: fa-s3-cloudtrail-query.sql
jsonBlocks.content:
SELECT eventtime, eventname, useridentity.arn, requestparameters['bucketName'] AS bucket_name, requestparameters['key'] AS object_key
FROM fa_s3_cloudtrail_logs
WHERE eventsource = 's3.amazonaws.com'
  AND requestparameters['bucketName'] = 'fa-s3-foundations-<ACCOUNT_ID>'
ORDER BY eventtime DESC
LIMIT 20;

consoleSteps.expectedResult: Athena returns the generated S3 data events and CloudWatch exposes bucket storage metrics.
consoleSteps.warning: Athena charges by data scanned; always use the supplied filters and LIMIT for this lab.

cliSteps.command: aws s3api create-bucket --bucket fa-s3-audit-<ACCOUNT_ID> --region eu-west-2 --create-bucket-configuration LocationConstraint=eu-west-2 --profile fa-s3

cliSteps.command: aws cloudtrail put-event-selectors --trail-name fa-s3-audit-trail --advanced-event-selectors file://fa-s3-data-events.json --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-s3

cliSteps.explanation: Start trail logging.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The command returns without an error.

cliSteps.command: aws athena start-query-execution --query-string file://fa-s3-cloudtrail-query.sql --query-execution-context Database=default --result-configuration OutputLocation=s3://fa-s3-audit-<ACCOUNT_ID>/athena-results/ --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-s3
cliSteps.explanation: Run the supplied filtered audit query after the table exists.
cliSteps.expectedResult: Record QueryExecutionId as [ATHENA_QUERY_ID].

cliSteps.command: aws athena get-query-results --query-execution-id [ATHENA_QUERY_ID] --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-s3
cliSteps.explanation: Read the completed result.
cliSteps.expectedResult: Rows include the harmless PutObject, GetObject, or DeleteObject test activity.

cliSteps.expectedResult: The response includes BucketSizeBytes or NumberOfObjects metric definitions after AWS publishes them.

tasks.title: Delete every S3 training resource safely

consoleSteps.title: Follow the final cleanup checklist in exact order
consoleSteps.instruction: Open the Cleanup section at the end of this Follow Along.

instructions.text: Open the Cleanup section at the end of this Follow Along.
Confirm every target begins with fa-s3- or matches a recorded placeholder from this lab.

Remove S3 notification destinations and EventBridge targets before deleting their SNS, SQS, or Lambda destinations.

Do not delete unrelated resources even if they appear beside the lab resources.
